newsitem.title: USA: Democrat Daschle optimistic on U.S. budget accord.
newsitem.headline: Democrat Daschle optimistic on U.S. budget accord.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said Thursday he was optimistic about an agreement on a plan to balance the federal budget.

Discussing the budget proposed by President Clinton, he told reporters: "I am more optimistic about our prospects for achieving success in our consideration of a balanced budget proposal now than I have been for a long time."

He said he based his optimism partly on the credibility of the budget proposal, the attitude of Republicans on working to achieve a meaningful budget proposal and the "desire of both sides to try get this done in a much more constructive way than we did in the 104th Congress."

Asked what major sticking points might be in consideration of the budget, he said they centered on the level of tax cuts, where Republicans wanted to cut more, and likely differences on entitlements such as Medicare and Medicaid.
He said he understood Republicans were concerned about the size of President Clinton's $51 billion education plan.
Daschle said, however, that there was not much difference between Democrats and Republicans on the defense budget.
He said both Republicans and Democrats were willig to work on a budget that did not contain any "smoke and mirrors."
